source_text:
# A STRESS DOMAIN, NOT AN EXAMPLE — lives under qa/stress_domains/, not
# examples/, on purpose (see qa/bluebook/quality_control.bluebook's own
# "being clever" note and .claude/skills/hecks_qa/SKILL.md's "Authoring a
# new stress domain" section).
#
# THE CONSTRUCT COMBINATION THIS DOMAIN IS FOR — ANGLE-9 (`ask backlog`,
# QualityControl ledger): `corrects` (retroactive correction) has exactly
# ONE declaration anywhere in the corpus, `examples/banking/bluebook/
# deposit_accounts.bluebook:353` (`Account.CorrectFee`), and it is
# AGGREGATE-level there — `reference_to Account`, not inside an `entity`
# block. `corrects` is also absent from `Hecks::Fuzzing::Properties::
# FEATURE_COVERAGE` entirely: no property anywhere has ever claimed the
# "Command#corrects" language feature. This domain puts `corrects` on an
# ENTITY-level command instead (`Entry.Amend`, below) — a combination
# checked directly against the whole corpus before writing this file
# (`grep -rn 'corrects ' examples/*/bluebook/*.bluebook qa/bluebook/*.
# bluebook qa/stress_domains/*/bluebook/*.bluebook` — one hit, the
# aggregate-level one above) — plus a whole-list `list_of(Entry)` COMMAND
# ARGUMENT (`Ledger.ReplaceEntries`, also a corpus first — `Hecks::
# Fuzzing::SequenceGenerator::StepBuilder#args_for`'s own comment says a
# list-of-ENTITY command attribute "has no real example anywhere in this
# repo's domains"), and a `remove:`-then-`append:` sequence on the same
# entity list (`Ledger.Void` / `Ledger.Record`), aimed at the
# `GUARANTEED_BY_CONSTRUCTION` note on `Entity#identified_by` in `lib/
# hecks/fuzzing/properties.rb` ("current.size + 1 can't repeat unless
# something remove:s from the list between mints, which no real domain
# does today").
#
# WHAT THIS DOMAIN FOUND, FIRST TRY — NOT FIXED HERE, reported to the QA
# orchestrator instead (see this domain's own NOTES.md for the full
# write-up and exact reproduction):
#
#   1. `Entry.Amend`'s own `corrects` mutation is UNCHECKED at build time
#      (`AggregateBuilder::Sealing#seal_correction_targets` walks only
#      `@commands` — the AGGREGATE's own top-level list — never
#      `@entities`, so an entity's own `corrects` mutation is invisible
#      to it) AND crashes at DISPATCH time: `EntityInterpreter#step_
#      enforce_givens` never calls `CommandRules::Admissibility#
#      enforce_correction_target` at all (only `CommandInterpreter`'s own
#      aggregate-level twin does), and `EntityElement.apply_to_element`'s
#      own `case mutation.op` has no `:corrects` branch — unlike
#      `MutationApplier#apply`'s aggregate-level twin, which treats it as
#      a documented no-op. Dispatching `Entry.Amend` therefore always
#      raises `Hecks::Runtime::WiringError` ("no entity mutation applier
#      handles :corrects — add one before declaring it"), which is NOT
#      one of `Hecks::Runtime::DOMAIN_REFUSALS` — it propagates straight
#      through `Fuzzing::Replay`'s own per-step isolation and crashes the
#      whole run, the same way an interpreter defect always does.
#
#   2. Because of (1), `EntryAmended` (the corrected event) can never be
#      EMITTED by Ruby at all — so `CorrectionWatch` (the process manager
#      below, reacting to it) and `FlaggedTrailCount` (the count read
#      model over what it flags) are both permanently dead code under
#      Ruby today, not merely untested. Kept anyway — they are exactly
#      what ANGLE-9's premise asked for ("a saga on the corrected event
#      and a count read-model over it"), and they are real, well-formed
#      declarations a future fix makes reachable rather than something
#      this domain would need to redeclare later.
#
#   3. `sets :entries, remove: :sequence` (`Ledger.Void`) is a silent
#      NO-OP against an entity-typed list, for an unrelated reason:
#      `Hecks::Runtime::Value::Coercion#for_attribute` routes ANY
#      `list_of` attribute through `#hydrate_entity_list` before it ever
#      asks whether the element type is an entity or a value object.
#      That method unconditionally does `Array(value).map { ... }` — no
#      `value.is_a?(Array)` guard, unlike its OWN value-object sibling
#      `#hydrate_value_object_list`, whose comment explains exactly why
#      that guard exists for `remove:`'s single-target value ("`Array(a_
#      Hash)` is NOT harmless... silently shredding a single-element
#      Hash-shaped target into garbage"). For an entity target the single
#      removal value is a scalar (`EntrySequence`), so `Array(value)`
#      wraps it into a one-element Array instead of shredding a Hash —
#      and `MutationApplier#removed`'s `Array(instance[target]).reject {
#      |element| element == value }` then compares each stored Hash
#      element against that wrapping Array, which can never be `==` a
#      Hash. Nothing is ever removed, and nothing refuses either.
#
#   4. Because of (3), the `remove:`-then-`append:` sequence this domain
#      was built to exercise (`GUARANTEED_BY_CONSTRUCTION`'s "current.
#      size + 1 can't repeat unless something remove:s from the list
#      between mints, which no real domain does today") cannot actually
#      happen on THIS domain, or on any domain, as things stand — not
#      because no real domain has tried it, but because `remove:` on an
#      entity list does not work at all yet. The comment's premise holds,
#      but only vacuously: see NOTES.md for the direct, by-hand
#      confirmation (`Ledger.Record` × 2, `Ledger.Void`, `Ledger.Record`
#      again — the list has 3 entries, not 2, and the "removed" one is
#      still there).
#
#   5. `Ledger.ReplaceEntries` (`sets :entries` bare, importing the
#      aggregate's own `list_of(Entry)` attribute onto the command
#      verbatim — `CommandBuilder#resolve_bare_set!`'s own shape,
#      `ConsoleSettings::Collection.ReplaceColumns`'s corpus precedent,
#      but for an ENTITY element type rather than a value object for the
#      first time) accepts a caller-supplied whole list with NO identity
#      check at all — `#hydrate_entity_list` rebuilds each element's own
#      declared fields but never runs `MutationApplier#check_entity_
#      collision`, the guard every OTHER way of adding an entity element
#      goes through. Two entries with the same `sequence` — or one with
#      none at all — both pass silently. See NOTES.md.
Hecks.bluebook "Corrections" do
  vision "A ledger of entries where one entry can be corrected after the fact — corrects declared on the entity owning the entry, not the aggregate, for the first time in the corpus — with a saga and a count read model watching the correction, and a remove-then-append sequence on the same entity list."

  core

  aggregate "Ledger" do
    description "A ledger holding entries, one of which may later be amended."

    identified_by :reference

    attribute :reference, LedgerReference
    attribute :entries,   list_of(Entry)

    value_object "LedgerReference" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a ledger is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    # POSITIVE-ONLY, same shape as `nested_pieces`' own `BoardNumber`/
    # `CardSequence` and `waybill`'s own `SlotNumber` — deliberately, so
    # an offered `0`/negative sequence is non-blank (survives routing)
    # and still fails the invariant once a typed rebuild is attempted.
    value_object "EntrySequence" do
      attribute :value, Integer
      invariant("an entry sequence is positive") { value.positive? }
    end

    value_object "EntryAmount" do
      attribute :cents, Integer
      invariant("an entry amount is positive") { cents.positive? }
    end

    command "Open" do
      role "Clerk"
      goal "Open a ledger"

      attribute :reference, LedgerReference

      emits "LedgerOpened"
    end

    command "Record" do
      role "Clerk"
      goal "Record a new entry on the ledger — the auto-minted half of the remove-then-append sequence"

      reference_to Ledger
      attribute :amount, EntryAmount

      sets :entries, append: { amount: :amount }

      emits "EntryRecorded"
    end

    # THE REMOVE HALF OF THE SEQUENCE THIS DOMAIN EXISTS TO EXERCISE —
    # see this file's own header comment, finding 3/4, and NOTES.md for
    # what actually happens (a confirmed silent no-op, not the identity-
    # reuse question this domain set out to ask).
    command "Void" do
      role "Clerk"
      goal "Remove an entry from the ledger outright"

      reference_to Ledger
      attribute :sequence, EntrySequence

      sets :entries, remove: :sequence

      emits "EntryVoided"
    end

    # THE CORPUS'S FIRST list_of(ENTITY) COMMAND ARGUMENT — every other
    # entity-owned list anywhere in this repository is populated one
    # element at a time via an append command (`Record`, above, and every
    # `AddX` in `nested_pieces`/`waybill`); nothing replaces the WHOLE
    # list in one dispatch the way `ConsoleSettings::Collection.
    # ReplaceColumns` already does for a `list_of(VALUE OBJECT)`. `sets
    # :entries` (bare) imports `Ledger`'s own declared `list_of(Entry)`
    # attribute onto this command verbatim, the identical mechanism
    # `ReplaceColumns` uses — untested for an ENTITY element type until
    # this domain. See this file's own header comment, finding 5, and
    # NOTES.md for what actually happens.
    command "ReplaceEntries" do
      role "Clerk"
      goal "Replace the ledger's whole list of entries at once"

      reference_to Ledger

      sets :entries

      emits "EntriesReplaced"
    end

    # A PIECE INSIDE THE LEDGER (ADR 0026) — `identified_by :sequence` is
    # auto-minted by `Record`'s own `append:` above (one past the highest
    # held sequence, `MutationApplier#next_identity`), the same
    # mechanism `nested_pieces`'/`waybill`'s own entity lists already
    # use.
    entity "Entry" do
      description "One recorded entry, whose amount can later be corrected."

      identified_by :sequence

      attribute :sequence, EntrySequence
      attribute :amount,   EntryAmount

      # THE ENTITY-LEVEL `corrects` COMMAND — THE WHOLE REASON THIS
      # DOMAIN EXISTS. `reason:` is required in practice
      # (`CommandBuilder#corrects_impl`'s own comment). `reference`
      # duplicates the LEDGER's own identity as an ordinary command
      # argument, purely so `EntryAmended`'s own payload carries it —
      # `CommandRules::Emission#emit`'s `payload: args` is the command's
      # OWN dispatch args, and an entity command's emitted event
      # otherwise carries none of the parent aggregate's own fields
      # (only `event.id`, read by nothing a `process_manager`'s own
      # `correlates_by` can name) — so `CorrectionWatch`, below, has a
      # dotted field to correlate on at all once this event can ever
      # actually fire. Not `sets`; nothing on `Entry` stores it.
      command "Amend" do
        role "Auditor"
        goal "Correct an entry's amount after it was recorded in error"

        attribute :reference, LedgerReference
        attribute :amount,    EntryAmount
        corrects "EntryRecorded", reason: "an entry amount was mis-keyed and needs correcting"

        sets :amount

        emits "EntryAmended"
      end
    end
  end

  # THE SECOND AGGREGATE A `CorrectionWatch` DISPATCH TARGETS —
  # rootless from `Ledger`'s own perspective on purpose (correlated only
  # by the shared `reference` field, the same convention `waybill`'s own
  # `Consignment`/`Manifest` pair already uses, redeclaring the identical
  # value-object NAME rather than sharing one aggregate-to-aggregate).
  aggregate "AuditTrail" do
    description "One flag raised against a ledger once one of its entries has been corrected."

    identified_by :reference

    attribute :reference, LedgerReference

    # REDECLARED, NOT SHARED — `waybill`'s own `SlotNumber`/`ItemLabel`
    # precedent: a value-object table is per-aggregate, so the SAME
    # correlation field name across two aggregates still needs its own
    # local copy of the type.
    value_object "LedgerReference" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a ledger is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "clean" do
      transition "Flag" => "flagged", from: "clean"
    end

    command "Open" do
      role "System"
      goal "Open an audit trail for a ledger"

      attribute :reference, LedgerReference

      emits "AuditTrailOpened"
    end

    command "Flag" do
      role "System"
      goal "Flag the audit trail once its ledger's own correction lands"

      reference_to AuditTrail

      emits "AuditTrailFlagged"
    end

    query "Flagged" do
      description "Audit trails already flagged by a landed correction."
      where(status: "flagged")
      order_by :reference
    end
  end

  # A COUNT READ MODEL OVER THE CORRECTION'S OWN EFFECT — ANGLE-9's own
  # premise ("a count read-model over it"). Rootless, like banking's own
  # `AccountsByKind` — a reviewer's question here ("how many corrections
  # have landed, across every ledger, right now") has no single ledger to
  # anchor it to. Answers 0 under Ruby today, always — see this file's
  # own header comment, finding 2: `AuditTrail::Flag` is reachable only
  # once `CorrectionWatch`'s own first leg delivers, which needs
  # `EntryAmended` to be emitted at all.
  read_model "FlaggedTrailCount" do
    description "How many audit trails have been flagged following a landed correction — a single number, not the rows themselves."
    include AuditTrail
    where(status: "flagged")
    count
  end

  # THE SAGA ON THE CORRECTED EVENT — ANGLE-9's own premise ("a process
  # manager on the corrected event"). `correlates_by :"reference.value"`
  # reads `Entry.Amend`'s own redundant `reference` argument (see that
  # command's own comment) on leg 1, and `AuditTrail`'s own identity
  # field on leg 2 — the same shared-field-name convention `waybill`'s
  # own `Packing` saga already uses across `Consignment`/`Manifest`.
  # PERMANENTLY UNREACHABLE UNDER RUBY TODAY (finding 2, this file's own
  # header comment) — kept, not removed, because it is exactly the
  # well-formed construct ANGLE-9 asked this domain to give first
  # coverage to, and a future fix to finding 1 makes it reachable with no
  # further authoring needed.
  process_manager "CorrectionWatch" do
    correlates_by :"reference.value"
    starts_on Ledger::EntryAmended
    ends_on   AuditTrail::AuditTrailFlagged

    transition Ledger::EntryAmended => "flagging", from: "flagging" do
      dispatch AuditTrail::Open, with: { reference: :reference }
    end

    transition AuditTrail::AuditTrailOpened => "flagging", from: "flagging" do
      dispatch AuditTrail::Flag, with: { reference: :reference }
    end
  end
end
